newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PEARCE EXPECTED TO QUIT AS CARETAKER-MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PEARCE EXPECTED TO QUIT AS CARETAKER-MANAGER.

text.p: England defender Stuart Pearce is set to stand down as caretaker-manager of relegated Nottingham Forest on Thursday.
Forest have called a mid-day news conference at their City Ground when the 35-year-old left-back is expected to officially announce he is handing over control to general manager Dave Bassett.
Pearce has been in charge since December 20 after former manager Frank Clark resigned following the club's poor start to the season.
Forest, European champions in 1979 and 1980, had won only one of their first 17 league matches at the start of the season and were bottom of the table when Clark departed.

But they pulled off a a shock 2-1 victory over Arsenal in Pearce's first game as caretaker manager and went on to win five of their next seven games, including a 2-1 F.A. Cup win at Newcastle on January 26.
But a run of just one win in the next 14 premier league games sentenced them to relegation. That was confirmed when they could only draw 1-1 at home with Wimbledon last Saturday.
Pearce had always planned to announce whether he wanted to stay in charge at the end of the season.
But he said on Wednesday: "I made up my mind some time ago.
"The fact we have now been relegated was irrelevant to my decision. I sat down and discussed the matter with my wife and made up my mind what was best for Stuart Pearce.
"I'm certain its also the right decision for the club."

He blames the long delay over the club's takeover by new owners, which had to be ratified by a series of shareholders meetings, for the club's ultimate demise, their second relegation from the premier league in four seasons.
"When you consider just how long it dragged on, the fact that money wasn't available for new players when it was needed, became critical." he said.
"From the magerial point of view, both Frank Clark and myself needed an injection of new players.
"By the time I was eventually able to sign one or two individuals it was probably too late."
